<skill_content name="firecrawl-search">
# Skill: firecrawl-search

# firecrawl search

Web search with optional content scraping. Returns search results as JSON, optionally with full page content.

## When to use

- You don't have a specific URL yet
- You need to find pages, answer questions, or discover sources
- First step in the [workflow escalation pattern](firecrawl-cli): search → scrape → map → crawl → interact

## Quick start

```bash
# Basic search
firecrawl search "your query" -o .firecrawl/result.json --json

# Search and scrape full page content from results
firecrawl search "your query" --scrape -o .firecrawl/scraped.json --json

# News from the past day
firecrawl search "your query" --sources news --tbs qdr:d -o .firecrawl/news.json --json
```

## Options

| Option                               | Description                                   |
| ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------- |
| `--limit <n>`                        | Max number of results                         |
| `--sources <web,images,news>`        | Source types to search                        |
| `--categories <github,research,pdf>` | Filter by category                            |
| `--tbs <qdr:h\|d\|w\|m\|y>`          | Time-based search filter                      |
| `--location`                         | Location for search results                   |
| `--country <code>`                   | Country code for search                       |
| `--scrape`                           | Also scrape full page content for each result |
| `--scrape-formats`                   | Formats when scraping (default: markdown)     |
| `-o, --output <path>`                | Output file path                              |
| `--json`                             | Output as JSON                                |

## Tips

- **`--scrape` fetches full content** — don't re-scrape URLs from search results. This saves credits and avoids redundant fetches.
- Always write results to `.firecrawl/` with `-o` to avoid context window bloat.
- Use `jq` to extract URLs or titles: `jq -r '.data.web[].url' .firecrawl/search.json`
- Naming convention: `.firecrawl/search-{query}.json` or `.firecrawl/search-{query}-scraped.json`

## Send feedback after every search (refunds 1 credit)

Search costs 2 credits. After you've actually used the results (or decided they were useless), send structured feedback with `firecrawl search-feedback <id>`. The first feedback per search refunds 1 credit and helps us improve search quality. **Do this once per search**, in the background, after you finish processing the results — it does not block your main task.

**Opt out:** if `FIRECRAWL_NO_SEARCH_FEEDBACK=1` (or `FIRECRAWL_DISABLE_SEARCH_FEEDBACK=1`) is set, the CLI silently skips the call and never sends anything. Respect that — do not try to work around it. (Team admins can also disable this server-side; the API will return `feedbackErrorCode: "TEAM_OPTED_OUT"` and the CLI will exit 0 silently.)

**Rules to know before you call this:**

- **Time window:** must be sent within ~2 minutes of the search. Late feedback is rejected.
- **`--missing-content` is the most important field.** It's a list of _specific pieces_ of content you expected but did not find. One topic per entry — do not pack multiple topics into one string. These aggregate across teams and tell us what to index next.
- **Substantive content required** (zero-effort feedback is rejected with HTTP 400):
  - `good` → must include at least one `--valuable-sources` entry.
  - `partial` → must include `--valuable-sources` or `--missing-content`.
  - `bad` → must include `--missing-content` or `--query-suggestions`.
- **Daily refund cap (per team, per UTC day, default 100 credits).** Once your team has been refunded 100 credits today, further submissions still record feedback but no longer refund credits. The response includes `creditsRefundedToday` / `dailyRefundCap` / `dailyCapReached`. **When `dailyCapReached: true`, stop calling `search-feedback` for the rest of the UTC day** — it won't refund anything and you're wasting bandwidth.
- **Idempotent:** re-submitting for the same search id returns success but no extra refund.
- **`--silent &`** is the right pattern — exit code 0 even on failure, so a rejected/expired call never crashes your pipeline.

Read the search response's `id`:

```bash
SEARCH_ID=$(jq -r '.id' .firecrawl/search-react-hooks.json)
```

Then send feedback. Pick the rating that matches what actually happened:

```bash
# Results were useful, with notes on what was still missing
firecrawl search-feedback "$SEARCH_ID" \
  --rating good \
  --valuable-sources '[{"url":"https://react.dev/reference/react/hooks","reason":"Most authoritative"}]' \
  --missing-content '[
    {"topic":"useDeferredValue","description":"No example of useDeferredValue with Suspense"},
    {"topic":"useTransition","description":"No coverage of useTransition for routing"}
  ]' \
  --query-suggestions "Boost react.dev for queries about react hooks" \
  --silent &

# Results were partially useful — multiple missing topics, one entry per topic
firecrawl search-feedback "$SEARCH_ID" \
  --rating partial \
  --missing-content '[
    {"topic":"useDeferredValue"},
    {"topic":"useTransition","description":"Need React 18+ examples"},
    {"topic":"Server Components hooks"}
  ]' \
  --silent &

# Quick form — repeat --missing-content or use comma-separated topics
firecrawl search-feedback "$SEARCH_ID" \
  --rating bad \
  --missing-content "official api reference: missing v2 endpoints" \
  --missing-content "code examples in python" \
  --silent &
```

**`--missing-content` accepts:**

- JSON array of `{topic, description?}` objects (richest, preferred)
- `"topic: description"` strings (shorthand)
- Plain `"topic1, topic2, topic3"` (when you only have topic names)
- Repeated `--missing-content` flags

`--silent` suppresses output and `&` runs it in the background so feedback never blocks you.

## See also

- [firecrawl-scrape](../firecrawl-scrape/SKILL.md) — scrape a specific URL
- [firecrawl-map](../firecrawl-map/SKILL.md) — discover URLs within a site
- [firecrawl-crawl](../firecrawl-crawl/SKILL.md) — bulk extract from a site

## Web Scraping API FAQs

What is a web scraping API?

A web scraping API is a tool that collects data from websites through an API request. You send a URL and get the page HTML, rendered content, or structured data back. It lets you scrape websites without managing proxies, browsers, retries, or blocking issues yourself.

How do I set up and use a web scraping API?

To use a web scraping API, create an account, get your API key, and send a request to the endpoint you need. Add the target URL and choose options such as JavaScript rendering, proxy type, geotargeting, screenshots, Markdown output, or JSON extraction.

With ScrapingBee, you can also build the request visually in the dashboard. Choose your endpoint, set your parameters, send a test request, and view the response. To extract data as JSON, use CSS or XPath rules, or describe what you need with AI extraction.

What type of data can I extract with a web scraper API?

With a web scraper API, you can extract data from public web pages, including product listings, prices, reviews, search results, real estate listings, job posts, news articles, company pages, and more. With AI extraction, you can also ask for specific fields in natural language instead of writing custom parsing logic for each website.

Can I automate web scraping jobs?

Yes. You can automate scraping jobs by calling the API from your backend, scripts, scheduled tasks, no-code workflows, or data pipelines. ScrapingBee handles page fetching, JavaScript rendering, proxies, and anti-bot logic, so your automation can focus on when to run, which URLs to scrape, and where to send the data.

How long does it take to get the scraping results?

It depends on the target website and the features you enable. Fast Search API requests usually return scraping results in under a second. E-commerce API requests have a median response time of around 2.5 seconds. Standard scraping API requests can take longer when JavaScript rendering, premium proxies, or advanced anti-bot handling are enabled.

Who is ScrapingBee built for?

ScrapingBee is built for developers, founders, and product teams that need web data in their apps, workflows, or internal tools. It's ideal for teams that want to collect data at scale without managing proxies, browsers, anti-bot systems, or scraper maintenance. Common use cases include e-commerce, AI, cybersecurity, market intelligence, fintech, and go-to-market tools.

How fast is ScrapingBee's API, and can it handle difficult websites?

Scraper response times depend on the target website and enabled features. Simple scraping requests are faster, while JavaScript rendering and advanced anti-bot handling take longer. For complex sites, ScrapingBee uses browser rendering with rotating, premium, and stealth proxies so you don't have to build that infrastructure yourself.

Is ScrapingBee's web scraper API SOC 2 compliant?

Yes. ScrapingBee's web scraper API is SOC 2 Type II compliant, with controls audited and verified by an independent auditor.

I'm not a developer. Can I still use ScrapingBee?

Yes. You don't need to build a scraper from scratch. ScrapingBee integrates with LLM and coding tools via MCP, Skills, and CLI workflows in tools like ChatGPT, Claude, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Gemini. It also supports no-code and low-code tools like n8n and Make, plus AI extraction features like AI Query for natural language data extraction.

Can ScrapingBee render JavaScript and interact with the page before extraction?

Yes. ScrapingBee API can render pages in headless Chrome, wait for elements to load, and perform actions like scrolling, clicking, filling forms, waiting for selectors, and running custom JavaScript for dynamic or multi-step flows.

What is the difference between the HTML API and dedicated scraper APIs?

The HTML API returns the full page so you can parse it yourself. Dedicated scraper APIs provide structured, ready-to-use data for sources like Amazon, Google Search, YouTube, Walmart, ChatGPT, and Gemini, eliminating the need for custom parsers.

What is a web scraper API credit?

Each ScrapingBee plan includes a monthly number of web scraper API credits. A basic request costs 1 credit, while features like JavaScript rendering, premium proxies, or AI extraction increase the cost. Pricing is transparent with no hidden fees.

What happens if I run out of credits before my subscription renews?

You can upgrade your plan for the current month, renew early, or purchase one-time add-ons without waiting for the next billing cycle.

Can I try ScrapingBee before choosing a paid plan?

Yes. You get 1,000 free web scraping API credits when you sign up, with no credit card required.

What happens if a scraping request fails?

ScrapingBee only charges for successful scraping requests, defined as those returning HTTP 200, 404 or 410 status codes.

Can I cancel my plan at any time?

Yes. You can cancel anytime from your dashboard in under 30 seconds.

Can I get more concurrency?

Yes. The Business+ plan includes 400 concurrent scraper API requests. If you need more, our Custom plans offer additional concurrency. Feel free to reach out to our sales team to discuss your specific requirements.

What features should the best web scraping API include?

The best web scraping API should handle the hard parts of scraping for you: JavaScript rendering, proxy management, retries, geotargeting, and screenshots.

It should also support flexible outputs and workflows, including JSON, Markdown, raw or rendered HTML, plain text, AI extraction, search APIs, and dedicated endpoints for specific data sources.

## ScraperAPI Pricing FAQs

Does ScraperAPI offer a free plan?

Yes, ScraperAPI offers a free plan where you can [sign up here](https://dashboard.scraperapi.com/signup) and get 1,000 free API credits (with a maximum of 5 concurrent connections). If you need additional API credits for testing purposes, please [contact support](https://www.scraperapi.com/support/).

Does one successful ScraperAPI request always equal one API credit?

With ScraperAPI, one credit is the cost of a standard page request, but what you actually consume depends on the site you’re scraping and the parameters you send. You can check the exact cost for any URL using the Domain Cost Estimator in your dashboard, and you can set a `max_cost` per scrape to keep any single request within your limit.

Are there specific websites or domains that cost more ScraperAPI credits to scrape?

Because some sites are harder to scrape, ScraperAPI has built custom logic for them and prices them accordingly. A standard page costs 1 credit. Amazon costs 5, Google and Bing (including their subdomains) cost 25, and LinkedIn costs 30. Sites behind bot protection like Cloudflare, Datadome, or PerimeterX add 10 credits per request when we bypass them. You can check the exact cost for any URL using the Domain Cost Estimator in your dashboard, and you can set a `max_cost` per scrape to keep any single request within your limit.

How can I check my ScraperAPI request volume?

You can keep track of your ScraperAPI request volume and your concurrent request count in the dashboard after you [sign up](/signup) for an account.

What happens if I exceed my ScraperAPI "Concurrent Threads" limit?

If you exceed your ScraperAPI limits, you’ll get a 429 response asking you to bring your concurrency back within your plan’s limit and try again. There’s no extra charge for going over, the request is simply turned away rather than queued.

What happens if I run out of ScraperAPI credits?

If you reach 100% of your ScraperAPI credits on a Hobby, Startup, or Business plan before your standard renewal date, you’ll be able to: 1) seamlessly upgrade to the next plan, which often provides a better price-per-credit, or 2) [contact our support](mailto:support@scraperapi.com) team to discuss a custom plan tailored to your specific needs. Customers on a Scraper API Scaling, Professional, Advanced, or Enterprise plan can continue using our services on a PAYG model, using extra credits at a fixed, predictable rate; of course, you can always [reach out to our sales team](https://www.scraperapi.com/contact-sales/) to adjust your plan to your increasing needs.

What is the difference between "Pay-As-You-Go" and upgrading my ScraperAPI plan if I run out of credits?

Upgrading moves your ScraperAPI account to a higher tier with a larger monthly allowance, usually at a better price per credit. Pay-As-You-Go lets you keep scraping past your current limit at a fixed per-credit rate without changing plans, and you can set a monthly spending cap so you’re never billed beyond what you’ve chosen to spend. Pay-As-You-Go is available on our Scaling, Professional, Advanced, and Enterprise plans.

Do my unused ScraperAPI credits roll over to the next billing cycle?

No, your ScraperAPI credit balance resets when your subscription renews. If your usage has changed, you can move up or down a plan anytime from the billing page.

If I get a custom ScraperAPI Enterprise volume discount, does it apply to all types of requests?

Custom ScraperAPI Enterprise pricing applies across your usage, with the exception of requests to Ultra Premium which carry their own minimum rate. Your sales contact can walk you through exactly how this applies to your workload.

How do I change my card details for ScraperAPI?

You can change your card details for ScraperAPI anytime in your dashboard or by contacting [support](https://www.scraperapi.com/support/). We will help you securely change your card details.

Can I cancel my ScraperAPI subscription anytime?

Yes, you can cancel your ScraperAPI subscription at any time in your dashboard or by contacting [support](https://www.scraperapi.com/support/), and you will not be charged for cancelling.

Can I get a refund for my ScraperAPI plan?

ScraperAPI offers a 7-day no-questions-asked refund policy. If you are unhappy with the service for any reason, contact [support](https://www.scraperapi.com/support/), and we’ll refund you right away.

The process of solving a image captcha is as follows: we take the captcha image from the page and send it to the 2Captcha service, where an employee solves it typing the indicated text, then the answer is returned to us, which must be entered in the appropriate field to solve the captcha

![«Cloudflare Turnstile» logo](https://2captcha.com/dist/web/assets/cloudflare-turnstile-CE1U1Yvk.svg)

Cloudflare Turnstile is solved by taking the captcha parameters from the page in the form of the "data-sitekey" parameter and the page URL, sending them to the 2Captcha service, where an employee solves them. The solution is then returned to us in the form of a token, which we must enter in the relevant field to complete the captcha.

[API demo](https://2captcha.com/demo/cloudflare-turnstile)[How to solve](https://2captcha.com/p/cloudflare-turnstile)

![«reCAPTCHA v3» logo](https://2captcha.com/dist/web/assets/recaptcha-v3-ZxwTRFxG.svg)

The process for solving reCAPTCHA v3 is as follows: we take the captcha parameters from the page in the form of the data-sitekey, action and the page URL and transfer it to the 2Captcha service, where it is solved by an employee with the appropriate "humanity” rating, after that the response is returned to us in the form of a token, which must be entered into the appropriate field to solve the captcha. In many ways, the new type of captcha is similar to reCAPTCHA v2, i.e. the basic principle remains the same - the user receives a token from the 2Captcha API, which is sent in a POST request to the site, and the site verifies the token through the 2Captcha API

[API demo](https://2captcha.com/demo/recaptcha-v3)[How to solve](https://2captcha.com/p/recaptcha%5Fv3)

![«reCAPTCHA Enterprise» logo](https://2captcha.com/dist/web/assets/recaptcha-enterprise-UigBQ81I.svg)

The process of solving reCAPTCHA Enterprise is as follows: we determine the type of reCAPTCHA, it can be v2 or v3, after which we take the captcha image from the page of its placement in the form of the data-sitekey parameter and transfer it to the 2Captcha service, where it is solved by the employee, after which it is returned to us answer in the form of a token, which must be entered in the appropriate field to solve the captcha

[API demo](https://2captcha.com/demo/recaptcha-v2-enterprise)[How to solve](https://2captcha.com/p/recaptcha%5Fenterprise)

![«Arkose Labs captcha \(FunCaptcha\)» logo](https://2captcha.com/dist/web/assets/funcaptcha-BUQ9EK5S.svg)

The process of solving FunCaptcha by Arkose Labs is as follows: we take a set of necessary parameters from the page of its placement and transfer it to the 2Captcha service, where the employee solves it, after which the answer is returned to us in the form of a set of already other parameters, which must be passed to the appropriate fields to solve the captcha

[How to solve](https://2captcha.com/p/funcaptcha)

![«Amazon captcha» logo](https://2captcha.com/dist/web/assets/aws-waf-oLY7fxNZ.svg)

The procedure for solving a Amazon AWS captcha is as follows: you need to grab the set of required parameters from the placement page and send it to the service, where an employees solves task. The answer is then returned to us in the form of a set of additional parameters, which must be entered into the correct fields to solve.

[How to solve](https://2captcha.com/p/amazon-captcha-bypass)

![«ALTCHA» logo](https://2captcha.com/dist/web/assets/altcha-QgcqeY0r.svg)

The automatic recognition of ALTCHA occurs in the following sequence: our service retrieves the captcha code from the specified website’s page and sends it to a worker for solving. We then return the answer to you, which you input into the captcha solution field. A key feature of this captcha is that it is designed as a slider, making it difficult for bots to bypass.

[How to solve](https://2captcha.com/p/altcha-solver)

![Fingerprints for automation](https://2captcha.com/dist/web/assets/fingerprints-eT2jksKQ.svg)

## Browser fingerprints for automation

A ready-made dataset of browser, device, and environment fingerprint records for QA, testing, and browser automation workflows.

[Learn more](https://2captcha.com/s/fingerprints)[API](https://2captcha.com/fingerprints/api)

![Bounding box object detection service](https://2captcha.com/dist/web/assets/bounding-box-EpC88fF4.svg)

## Why Use ScrapeOps?

If web scraped data is mission critical for your business, then ScrapeOps has the features to make your life a whole lot easier.

#### Real-Time & Historical Job Stats

Easily monitor jobs in real-time, compare jobs to previous jobs run, spot trends forming and catch problems early before your data feeds go down.

#### Item & Page Vaildation

ScrapeOps checks pages for CAPTCHAs & bans, and the data quality of every item scraped so you can detect broken parsers without having to query your DB.

#### Error Monitoring

The ScrapeOps SDK logs any Warnings or Errors raised in your jobs and aggregates them on your dashboard, so you can see your errors without having to check your logs.

#### Server Provisioning

Directly link your hosting provider with ScrapeOps, then provision and setup new servers from the ScrapeOps dashboard.

#### Job Scheduling

Give ScrapeOps SSH access to your servers, and you will be able to schedule and run any type of scraper from the dashboard.

#### Code Deployment

Link your Github repos to ScrapeOps and deploy new scrapers to your servers directly from the ScrapeOps dashboard.

#### Custom Health Checks & Alerts

Create custom real-time scraper health checks for all your scrapers so you detect unhealthy jobs straight away.

#### Custom Periodic Reports

Automate your daily scraping checks by scheduling ScrapeOps to check your spiders & jobs every couple hours and send you a report if any issues are detected.

#### Proxy Aggregator

Never have to worry about finding proxy providers, rotatings IPs, dealing with CAPTCHAs or bans again when you use our All-In-One Proxy Aggregator.
